newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF won't comment on external reserves slip.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF won't comment on external reserves slip.

text.p: Japan's external reserves fell in January from the previous month, the first such slip in three years, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Monday, but a ministry official declined to comment on reasons for the fall.
The ministry said earlier on Monday that Japan's external reserves stood at $217.14 billion at the end of January compared with $217.87 billion in December.
Asked whether the decrease was due to dollar-selling intervention in the foreign exchange market in an attempt to halt the dollar's rise, the official said he could not comment.
The decrease may be partly due to transactions carried out with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the official said, declining to give further details.
Despite the decrease, Japan's external reserves still remain the largest in the world, followed by those of China, Germany, Taiwan and the United States, the official said.
It was the first decrease in Japan's external reserves in 39 months, the official said.
